OpenRouter

A deliberate model-routing layer.

OOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Access supported model providers through a unified API and configure routing around the task's requirements. MoreSpace can build a model gateway for content, extraction, and assistant products, with explicit provider choices, fallbacks, and spend reporting. We compare models on your own acceptance examples before deciding where lower cost, better output, or a fallback is useful.

Useful outputs

  • Model responses under shared integration
  • Routing and usage records
  • Comparison reports for model selection

Where we can apply it

  • Campaign request → evaluated model route → editor approval → content queue.
  • Extraction job → preferred provider → bounded fallback → validated record.
  • Evaluation sample → model comparison → acceptance review → routing configuration.
01

Use case 1

Route content and extraction tasks to evaluated models.

02

Use case 2

Add bounded fallback behavior when a selected provider fails.

03

Use case 3

Compare quality, latency, and cost across approved model candidates.

Inputs we need

  • Task-specific prompts and schemas
  • An approved provider allowlist
  • Quality and operating-cost targets

Delivery sequence

  • Evaluate candidate models against labeled business examples.
  • Configure allowed providers, fallback order, and spending controls.
  • Track quality and failures so routing decisions can be revised with evidence.

Expert review points

  • Confirm fallback providers meet the same data and feature requirements.
  • Compare accepted outputs rather than selecting solely by headline price.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • LangChain
  • OpenAI SDK-compatible clients
  • n8n
  • Custom applications

Signals we can make visible

  • Cost per accepted result
  • Task success rate
  • Provider error rate
  • Response latency

We agree the source, population, period, denominator, and decision behind each measure.
